wikiNodes.title: Elos
wikiNodes.body:
<!-- content-meta:eyJzdWJ0aXRsZSI6IkdvZCBvZiBUaGUgUGF0aCBvZiBCZWNvbWluZyIsInByb25vdW5zIjoiSGUvVGhleSIsImdlbmRlciI6Ik1hbGUiLCJ0eXBlIjoiTGVzc2VyIERlaXR5Iiwic3VwcHJlc3NlZE1lbnRpb25zIjpbImd1aWRhbmNlLXhwaGIiXX0= -->

Long ago, before paths were worn into the earth and before maps charted the lands, the world of Shivath was vast and unknown. In those times, travelers journeyed without guidance, and many became lost in the wilderness of their own fear and uncertainty. Among the gods, one being emerged to lead those who sought new **selves**—to discover and forge identities through the process of journeying.

This was **Elos**, a lesser deity whose influence shaped the inner transformations that accompany every great journey.  

It is said that **Elos** began his life as a mortal, born into a world that did not reflect their inner truth. In his heart, he knew that their true self was waiting at the end of a long journey. With courage, they left behind the life he was told to live and set off, crossing the vast lands and seas of Shivath, the Angra Mainyu and beyond, learning from every trial, reshaping themselves in body and soul until, at last, he emerged not as the person they were born, but as the person he **knew themselves to be**. In completing his journey, Elos ascended into the divine realm, vowing to **guide and protect others** who walk the path of transformation.  

In the world of **Shivath**, there is an ancient tradition known as **The Path of Becoming**, a revered journey inspired by Elos’ own odyssey. This **sacred pilgrimage** involves traveling from one significant location to another, often through varied and challenging terrains, with the purpose of **renouncing the old self and embracing the new**. Those who embark on this journey may do so for a variety of reasons: spiritual, physical, or emotional transformation. Many people in Shivath honor this tradition as a form of **rebirth**, choosing to emerge in a new place, recognized in their **true form**.

The **Path of Becoming** is a gift: an opportunity for those who seek to step into the world as their **authentic selves**. The journey itself is deeply personal, and no two paths are the same. For some, the journey is long and arduous, symbolizing the internal struggle that comes with self-acceptance. For others, it is a brief but powerful transition, a moment of clarity in which the old constraints are shed, and the true self is celebrated.

At the end of the path, there is often a **Rite of Becoming**, a communal or personal ritual where the traveler is welcomed by a new community or by those they hold dear, honoring their **transformation**. This rite is a moment of **rebirth into a world that acknowledges and respects their true identity**.

  

* * *

**Divine Domains:** [Travel](/dossiers/travel), [Freedom](/dossiers/freedom), [Stars](/dossiers/stars)

**Other Titles:** The Guiding Star, The Wanderer, The Ferryman

**Divine Symbols & Sigils:** A star on the horizon with a winding path crossing diagonally beneath it

**Church Boon: +1 Wisdom**

**Lip Service:** Proficiency in **Survival**

wikiNodes.title: The Red Hunter
wikiNodes.body:
<!-- content-meta: -->

He wasn’t always this—a thing of ash, rage, and ruin. Once, he was a man. A soldier. A tiefling with sharp horns and sharper eyes, marching under the artificer banners of Treftiel. He believed, in his quiet, stoic way, that he was fighting for something greater than himself: progress, civilization, a future built from steel and ingenuity. He was no hero, no champion. Just a body in the endless machinery of war.

The war was apocalyptic. The druids, wielding the raw fury of the earth, unleashed hurricanes of bark and root against the artificers’ gleaming, relentless machines. In the final battle, amidst the storms and fire, the soldier’s gun fired a single, desperate shot. It pierced chaos, struck something ancient, and ended the war.

The Red. A primordial force older than trees, older than machines. It crawled into his veins without asking, consuming him with fire that could not be extinguished. The artificers won the war, and the soldier returned to Treftiel not as a victor, but as a vessel for something terrible.

At first, the people hailed him as a savior. But the nobles, the king—they knew what he had become. The Red was not a trophy to celebrate, but a weapon to fear. And what is fear if not something to be controlled? They saw in him a lowly tiefling with a power they believed should belong to a king, to the throne of Treftiel. Their fear became jealousy. Jealousy became betrayal.

A celebration was called in his honor, grand and glittering. Wine poured like rivers, silverware gleamed under chandelier light, and his name was toasted with false smiles. He should have known better. Should have seen the knives behind the laughter, the poison in the cups. But he didn’t. He wanted to believe in them. In the people he had fought to protect.

The betrayal was savage. They came at him with blades, with gunfire, with all the greed and ambition of a kingdom that consumes even its own. The Red answered. It didn’t ask for permission, didn’t care for hesitation. Fire erupted from his veins, turning the feast into an inferno. Noble blood boiled. Machines melted like wax. When the smoke cleared, the halls of Treftiel lay in ruins, and the soldier they had betrayed was gone.

He became the **Red Hunter**, a creature of molten rage and grim purpose.

Now, he walks the scorched ruins of Shivath, his form a shadow wreathed in crimson fire. He has no love, no hatred, no loyalty. Only a singular goal: **to see Treftiel burn.** Not just its towers, its machines, its wealth—but its people. Its memory. Its name. The betrayal runs too deep to settle for anything less than complete obliteration.

He sees Treftiel not as a place, but as a disease—a sickness carried in the blood of nobles and passed down through their children. Generations of complicity and ambition. They are all guilty. Every one of them. And guilt demands fire.

His warlocks flock to him like moths, drawn to the light of his power. They think they understand his pain, his purpose, but they don’t. They can’t. They are scavengers, feeding off his flames. And he lets them. He gives them pieces of the Red, knowing they will use it for their own designs. He doesn’t care.

Because he knows what comes next.

When Treftiel is nothing more than a memory, when its last stone crumbles into dust, his warlocks will turn their guns on him. The Red will demand it. The cycle will demand it. They will kill him, and one of them will take his place. He waits for that day, for the moment when the flames he carries will finally consume him. But not yet.

Not until the last noble name has been forgotten. Not until the last story of Treftiel dies. Not until the Red has had its full due.

wikiNodes.title: Ranger
wikiNodes.body:
##### Core Traits

Primary Ability: Dexterity and Wisdom

Hit Point Die: D10 per Ranger level

Hit Points at Level 1: 10 + Con. modifier

Hit Points per additional Ranger Level: D10 + your Con. modifier, or, 6 + your Con. modifier

Saving Throw Proficiencies: Strength,Dexterity

Skill Proficiencies: Choose 3: Animal Handling, Athletics, Insight, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Stealth, or Survival.

Weapon Proficiencies: [Simple](https://5e.tools/items.html#blankhash,flsttype:simple%20weapon=1) and [Martial weapons](https://5e.tools/items.html#blankhash,flsttype:martial%20weapon=1)

Armor Training: [Light](https://5e.tools/items.html#blankhash,flsttype:light%20armor=1) and [Medium armor](https://5e.tools/items.html#blankhash,flsttype:medium%20armor=1) and [Shields](https://5e.tools/items.html#shield_xphb)

Starting Equipment: Choose A or B: (A) [Studded Leather Armor](https://5e.tools/items.html#studded%20leather%20armor_xphb), [Scimitar](https://5e.tools/items.html#scimitar_xphb), [Shortsword](https://5e.tools/items.html#shortsword_xphb), [Longbow](https://5e.tools/items.html#longbow_xphb), [20 Arrows](https://5e.tools/items.html#arrows%20\(20\)_xphb), [Quiver](https://5e.tools/items.html#quiver_xphb), [Druidic Focus](https://5e.tools/items.html#druidic%20focus_xphb) ([sprig of mistletoe](https://5e.tools/items.html#sprig%20of%20mistletoe_xphb)), [Explorer's Pack](https://5e.tools/items.html#explorer's%20pack_xphb), and 7 GP; or (B) 150 GP

##### Multiclassing

To qualify for a new class, you must have a score of at least 13 in the primary ability of the new class and your current classes.

Skill Proficiencies: Choose 1: Animal Handling, Athletics, Insight, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Stealth, or Survival.

Weapon Proficiencies: [Martial weapons](https://5e.tools/items.html#blankhash,flsttype:martial%20weapon=1)

Armor Training: [Light](https://5e.tools/items.html#blankhash,flsttype:light%20armor=1) and [Medium armor](https://5e.tools/items.html#blankhash,flsttype:medium%20armor=1) and [Shields](https://5e.tools/items.html#shield_xphb)

## Level 1: Spellcasting

You have learned to channel the magical essence of nature to cast spells. See [chapter 7](https://5e.tools/book.html#XPHB,7) for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Ranger spells, which appear in the [Ranger spell list](https://5e.tools/spells.html#blankhash,flstclass:ranger=1) later in the class's description.

Spell Slots. The Ranger Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a [Long Rest](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#long%20rest_xphb).

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two [level 1 Ranger spells](https://5e.tools/spells.html#blankhash,flstclass:ranger=1,flstlevel:1=1). [Cure Wounds](https://5e.tools/spells.html#cure%20wounds_xphb) and [Ensnaring Strike](https://5e.tools/spells.html#ensnaring%20strike_xphb) are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Ranger levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Ranger Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Ranger spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Ranger Features table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 5 Ranger, your list of prepared spells can include six Ranger spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination.

If another Ranger feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Ranger spells for you.

Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you finish a [Long Rest](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#long%20rest_xphb), you can replace one spell on your list with another Ranger spell for which you have spell slots.

Spellcasting Ability. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Ranger spells.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use a [Druidic Focus](https://5e.tools/items.html#druidic%20focus_xphb) as a [Spellcasting Focus](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#spellcasting%20focus_xphb) for your Ranger spells.

## Level 1: Favored Enemy

You always have the [Hunter's Mark](https://5e.tools/spells.html#hunter's%20mark_xphb) spell prepared. You can cast it twice without expending a spell slot, and you regain all expended uses of this ability when you finish a [Long Rest](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#long%20rest_xphb).

The number of times you can cast the spell without a spell slot increases when you reach certain Ranger levels, as shown in the Favored [Enemy](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#enemy_xphb) column of the Ranger Features table.

## Level 1: Weapon Mastery

Your training with weapons allows you to use the [mastery properties](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#weapon%20mastery%20properties_xphb) of two kinds of [weapons](https://5e.tools/items.html#blankhash,flsttype:simple%20weapon=1~martial%20weapon=1) of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as [Longbows](https://5e.tools/items.html#longbow_xphb) and [Shortswords](https://5e.tools/items.html#shortsword_xphb).

Whenever you finish a [Long Rest](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#long%20rest_xphb), you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the [mastery properties](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#weapon%20mastery%20properties_xphb) of [Scimitars](https://5e.tools/items.html#scimitar_xphb) and [Longswords](https://5e.tools/items.html#longsword_xphb).

## Level 2: Deft Explorer

Thanks to your travels, you gain the following benefits.

Expertise. Choose one of your skill proficiencies with which you lack [Expertise](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#expertise_xphb). You gain [Expertise](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#expertise_xphb) in that skill.

Languages. You know two languages of your choice from the language tables in [chapter 2](https://5e.tools/book.html#XPHB,2,choose%20languages,0).

## Level 2: Fighting Style

You gain a [Fighting Style feat](https://5e.tools/feats.html#blankhash,flstcategory:fs=1) of your choice. Instead of choosing one of those feats, you can choose the option below.

Druidic Warrior. You learn two [Druid cantrips](https://5e.tools/spells.html#blankhash,flstlevel:0=1,flstclass:druid=1) of your choice. [Guidance](https://5e.tools/spells.html#guidance_xphb) and [Starry Wisp](https://5e.tools/spells.html#starry%20wisp_xphb) are recommended. The chosen cantrips count as Ranger spells for you, and Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for them. Whenever you gain a Ranger level, you can replace one of these cantrips with another Druid cantrip.

## Level 3: Ranger Subclass

You gain a Ranger subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Ranger levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Ranger level or lower.

###   

## Level 4: Ability Score Improvement

You gain the [Ability Score Improvement](https://5e.tools/feats.html#ability%20score%20improvement_xphb) feat or another [feat](https://5e.tools/feats.html) of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Ranger levels 8, 12, and 16.

## Level 5: Extra Attack

You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the [Attack](https://5e.tools/actions.html#attack_xphb) action on your turn.

## Level 6: Roving

Your [Speed](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#speed_xphb) increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing Heavy armor. You also have a [Climb Speed](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#climb%20speed_xphb) and a [Swim Speed](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#swim%20speed_xphb) equal to your [Speed](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#speed_xphb).

## Level 7: Subclass FeatureP

You gain a feature from your Ranger Subclass.

###   

## Level 8: Ability Score Improvement

You gain the [Ability Score Improvement](https://5e.tools/feats.html#ability%20score%20improvement_xphb) feat or another [feat](https://5e.tools/feats.html) of your choice for which you qualify.

## Level 9: Expertise

Choose two of your skill proficiencies with which you lack [Expertise](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#expertise_xphb). You gain [Expertise](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#expertise_xphb) in those skills.

## Level 10: Tireless

Primal forces now help fuel you on your journeys, granting you the following benefits.

### Temporary Hit Points

As a [Magic](https://5e.tools/actions.html#magic_xphb) action, you can give yourself a number of [Temporary Hit Points](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#temporary%20hit%20points_xphb) equal to 1d8 plus your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1). You can use this action a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a [Long Rest](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#long%20rest_xphb).

### Decrease Exhaustion

Whenever you finish a [Short Rest](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#short%20rest_xphb), your [Exhaustion](https://5e.tools/conditionsdiseases.html#exhaustion_xphb) level, if any, decreases by 1.

## Level 11: True Hunter's Mark  

Whenever you start casting the Hunter's Mark spell, you can modify it so that it doesn't require [Concentration](https://5e.tools/conditionsdiseases.html#concentration_xphb). If you do so, the spell's duration becomes 1 minute for that casting.

  

## Level 11: Subclass Feature  

You gain a feature from your Ranger Subclass.

###   

## Level 12: Ability Score Improvement

You gain the [Ability Score Improvement](https://5e.tools/feats.html#ability%20score%20improvement_xphb) feat or another [feat](https://5e.tools/feats.html) of your choice for which you qualify.

## Level 13: Relentless Hunter

You ignore all Difficult Terrain, and your Speed cannot be reduced by any spell or effect.

## Level 14: Nature's Veil

You invoke spirits of nature to magically hide yourself. As a [Bonus Action](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#bonus%20action_xphb), you can give yourself the [Invisible](https://5e.tools/conditionsdiseases.html#invisible_xphb) condition until the end of your next turn.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a [Long Rest](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#long%20rest_xphb).

## Level 15: Subclass Feature

You gain a feature from your Ranger Subclass.

###   

## Level 16: Ability Score Improvement

You gain the [Ability Score Improvement](https://5e.tools/feats.html#ability%20score%20improvement_xphb) feat or another [feat](https://5e.tools/feats.html) of your choice for which you qualify.

## Level 17: Precise Hunter

You have [Advantage](https://5e.tools/variantrules.html#advantage_xphb) on attack rolls against the creature currently marked by your Hunter's Mark.

## Level 18: Feral Senses

Your connection to the forces of nature grants you Blindsight with a range of 30 feet.

## Level 19: Epic Boon

You gain an [Epic Boon feat](https://5e.tools/feats.html#blankhash,flstcategory:eb=1) or another [feat](https://5e.tools/feats.html) of your choice for which you qualify. [Boon of Dimensional Travel](https://5e.tools/feats.html#boon%20of%20dimensional%20travel_xphb) is recommended.

## Level 20: Hunter's Arsenal

Conjure Volley and Steel Wind Strike are added to your Ranger spell list. You can cast each of these spells once without expending a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest.

wikiNodes.title: Keepers of The Archive
wikiNodes.body:
The Keepers of the Archive are an esteemed group of mages and warriors, inspired by the ideals of preservation and the mastery of arcane magic. Their mission has always been twofold: to safeguard the collective magical knowledge of the world and to ensure its supremacy for the greater good. Driven by an insatiable thirst for knowledge, they dedicated themselves to collecting every book and tome, believing that knowledge was the ultimate path to enlightenment and power.

However, the unity of the Keepers was shattered following the mysterious disappearance of their enigmatic creator. In the aftermath, the faction fractured into various groups, each interpreting the original vision in their own way. Among these splintered factions, one has risen to prominence, led by Laris, a former chronicler of the Archive. Under Laris' guidance, this faction seeks to uphold the creator's original will, striving to reunite the scattered knowledge and restore the Archive to its former glory.

*Source: Eberron: Forge of the Artificer (2025-12-09)*

## Features

## Level 1: Spellcasting

You have learned how to channel magical energy through objects. See the Player's Handbook for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Artificer spells, which appear in the Artificer spell list later in the class's description.

### Tools Required

You produce your Artificer spells through tools. You can use Thieves' Tools, Tinker's Tools, or another kind of Artisan's Tools with which you have proficiency as a Spellcasting Focus, and you must have one of those focuses in hand when you cast an Artificer spell (meaning the spell has an M component when you cast it).

### Cantrips

You know two Artificer cantrips of your choice. Acid Splash and Prestidigitation are recommended.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Artificer cantrip of your choice.

When you reach Artificer levels 10 and 14, you learn another Artificer cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Artificer Features table.

### Spell Slots

The Artificer Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

### Prepared Spells of Level 1+

You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Artificer spells. Cure Wounds and Grease are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Artificer levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Artificer Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Artificer spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 5 Artificer, your list of prepared spells can include six Artificer spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.

If another Artificer feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Artificer spells for you.

### Changing Your Prepared Spells

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with other Artificer spells for which you have spell slots.

### Spellcasting Ability

Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Artificer spells.

## Level 1: Tinker's Magic

You know the Mending cantrip.

As a Magic action while holding Tinker's Tools, you can create one item in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of yourself, choosing the item from the following list:

- Ball Bearings
- Basket
- Bedroll
- Bell
- Blanket
- Block and Tackle
- Glass Bottle
- Bucket
- Caltrops
- Candle
- Crowbar
- Flask
- Grappling Hook
- Hunting Trap
- Jug
- Lamp
- Manacles
- Net
- Oil
- Paper
- Parchment
- Pole
- Pouch
- Rope
- Sack
- Shovel
- Iron Spikes
- String
- Tinderbox
- Torch
- Vial

See the rules for the item in the Player's Handbook. The item lasts until you finish a Long Rest, at which point it vanishes.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

## Level 2: Replicate Magic Item

You have learned arcane plans that you use to make magic items.

### Plans Known

When you gain this feature, choose four plans to learn from the Magic Item Plans (Artificer Level 2+) table (see the Dungeon Master's Guide for the items' descriptions). Bag of Holding, Cap of Water Breathing, Sending Stones, and +1 Wand of the War Mage are recommended. Whenever you gain an Artificer level, you can replace one of the plans you know with a new plan for which you qualify.

You learn another plan of your choice when you reach certain Artificer levels, as shown in the Plans Known column of the Artificer Features table. When you choose a plan to learn, you choose it from any Magic Item Plans table for which you qualify; your qualification is based on your Artificer level.

### Creating an Item

When you finish a Long Rest, you can create one or two different magic items if you have Tinker's Tools in hand. Each item is based on one of the plans you know for this feature.

If a created item requires Attunement, you can attune yourself to it the instant you create it. If you decide to attune to the item later, you must do so using the normal process for Attunement.

When you reach certain Artificer levels specified in the Magic Items column of the Artificer Features table, the number of magic items you can create at the end of a Long Rest increases. Each item you create must be based on a different plan you know.

You can't have more magic items from this feature than the number shown in the Magic Items column of the Artificer Features table for your level. If you try to exceed your maximum number of magic items for this feature, the oldest item vanishes, and then the new item appears.

### Duration

A magic item created by this feature functions as the normal magic item, except its magic isn't permanent; when you die, the magic item vanishes after 1d4 days. If you replace a plan you know with a new plan, any magic item created with the replaced plan immediately vanishes.

If an item that you created with this feature is a container, such as a Bag of Holding, and it vanishes, its contents harmlessly appear in and around its space.

### Spellcasting Focus

You can use any Wand or Weapon created by this feature as a Spellcasting Focus in lieu of using a set of Artisan's Tools.

> **Crafting More Magic Items**
>
> The Replicate Magic Item feature isn't the only way for an Artificer to make magic items. The Dungeon Master's Guide provides rules for characters—not just Artificers—who want to make magic items of all sorts. Though many different characters can make magic items, Artificers can do it faster than others; each Artificer subclass improves a character's speed at making items of a certain category.
>
> When an Artificer crafts a magic item using the normal rules in the Dungeon Master's Guide, the character gains no special connection to that item. Class features that refer to items created by your Replicate Magic Item feature don't apply to items you craft by other means.

## Level 4: Ability Score Improvement

You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Artificer levels 8, 12, and 16.

## Level 6: Magic Item Tinker

Your Replicate Magic Item feature gains the following options.

### Charge Magic Item

As a Bonus Action, you can touch a magic item within 5 feet of yourself that you created with Replicate Magic Item and that uses charges. You expend a level 1+ spell slot and recharge the item. The number of charges the item regains is equal to the level of spell slot expended.

### Drain Magic Item

As a Bonus Action, you can touch a magic item within 5 feet of yourself that you created with Replicate Magic Item and cause the item to vanish, converting its magical energy into a spell slot. The slot is level 1 if the item is Common or level 2 if the item is Uncommon or Rare. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest. Any spell slot you create with this feature vanishes when you finish a Long Rest.

### Transmute Magic Item

As a Magic action, you can touch one magic item within 5 feet of yourself that you created with Replicate Magic Item and transform it into a different magic item. The resulting item must be based on a magic item plan you know. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

## Level 7: Flash of Genius

When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you fails an ability check or a saving throw, you can take a Reaction to add a bonus to the roll, potentially causing it to succeed. The bonus equals your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).

You can take this Reaction a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

## Level 8: Ability Score Improvement

You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

## Level 10: Magic Item Adept

You can now attune to up to four magic items at once.

## Level 11: Spell-Storing Item

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can touch one Simple or Martial weapon or one item that you can use as a Spellcasting Focus, and you store a spell in it, choosing a level 1, 2, or 3 Artificer spell that has a casting time of an action and doesn't require a Material component that is consumed by the spell (you needn't have the spell prepared).

While holding the object, a creature can take a Magic action to produce the spell's effect from it, using your spellcasting ability modifier. If the spell requires Concentration, the creature must concentrate. Once a creature has used the object to produce the spell's effect, the object can't be used this way again until the start of the creature's next turn.

The spell stays in the object until it's been used a number of times equal to twice your Intelligence modifier (minimum of twice) or until you use this feature again to store a spell in an object.

## Level 12: Ability Score Improvement

You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

## Level 14: Advanced Artifice

You gain the following benefits.

### Magic Item Savant

You can now attune to up to five magic items at once.

### Refreshed Genius

When you finish a Short Rest, you regain one expended use of your Flash of Genius feature.

## Level 16: Ability Score Improvement

You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

## Level 18: Magic Item Master

You can now attune to up to six magic items at once.

## Level 19: Epic Boon

You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Energy Resistance is recommended.

## Level 20: Soul of Artifice

You have developed a mystical connection to your magic items, which you can draw on for aid. You gain the following benefits.

### Cheat Death

If you're reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, you can disintegrate any number of Uncommon or Rare magic items created by your Replicate Magic Item feature. If you do so, your Hit Points instead change to a number equal to 20 times the number of magic items disintegrated.

### Magical Guidance

When you finish a Short Rest, you regain all expended uses of your Flash of Genius if you have Attunement to at least one magic item.

wikiNodes.title: Fódhla
wikiNodes.body:
<!-- content-meta: -->

What is known about Fódhla fits in the margins of the institution he founded.

In the rare documents that name him, he is credited as the founder of the Registry. The Registry existed as his idea before it existed as anything else. Its Ledger — the intelligence archive operatives consult to know the ground before they stand on it — came later, built by his husband [[Marcus Halberstram]]. Fódhla gave the Registry its purpose. Marcus gave it its memory.

The Registry takes contracts. It does not ask what the contract is for, or who is asking. A senator and a criminal walk in with the same offer; the Registry evaluates both on the same terms: can you pay, will you honor the agreement. That is all. Political standing, reputation, history — none of it enters the calculation.

That philosophy is Fódhla's. He built the institution on it and has never seen reason to revise it.

People who spend years in the Registry may never encounter him. He does not attend briefings. He does not run operations. When he does appear — silver-haired, unhurried, looking at something just past whoever is speaking to him — people notice. Not because of ceremony; there is none. But no one who has been there forgets it. Something in the Registry was about to change.

The contracts that bind operatives to the Registry are not a formality. They carry weight most people cannot lift. Fódhla can decide otherwise. No one else can. He does not do it often. When he does, it is not a negotiation.

His private life is not in the record. He is close to [[Marcus Halberstram]] in a way he is close to no one else. The weight those agreements carry comes from Marcus; what Fódhla can do with that weight is a separate matter. The Ledger does not go into it. What Fódhla keeps to himself, he tells Marcus.

## Handler's note

*Active classification: Confidential. Further records restricted to senior staff.*

*If you are reading this, you were meant to.*

wikiNodes.body:
<!-- content-meta:eyJzdWJ0aXRsZSI6IlRoZSBMb3N0IFNjaG9sYXIiLCJwcm9ub3VucyI6IkhlL0hpbSIsImdlbmRlciI6Ik1hbGUiLCJ0eXBlIjoiUGF0cm9uIChVbmRlYWQpIn0= -->

Whispers among scholars and tales shared under starlit skies speak of **Valdros, The Lost Scholar**, a patron who offers power to those brave enough to confront the truths hidden in the dark. In life, Valdros was an archmage driven by an obsession to understand the boundaries between light and shadow. His pursuit led him to a forbidden ritual that transformed him into an immortal lich. Yet, unlike others of his kind, Valdros did not succumb to the cold hunger for power; instead, he awakened with a vision: redemption and the acceptance of duality within every soul.

Valdros teaches that true strength comes from embracing both the shadow and light within oneself. His followers believe that redemption and freedom lie in confronting one's deepest fears and accepting the truth of who they are. Those who forge a pact with him gain powers that blend the protection of light and the ferocity of shadow, walking the fine line between mortality and eternity.

  

“Only by accepting your shadow will you find true redemption.”

wikiNodes.title: Morrigan
wikiNodes.body:
<!-- content-meta: -->

Morrigan handles the Registry's S-rank operations and above. Routine commissions don't usually reach her. When the Registry assigns her to something, the operation sits outside what standard operatives are expected to come back from.

How long she has been in the organization is hard to say. Most people who deal with the Registry know her name before they see her face. The ones who have worked near her don't usually bring it up.

Her mysterious yellow eyes are unsettling for most people. She looks at you like she's already past the moment you're in, reading something ahead of it. When asked direct questions, she answers obliquely (don't read it as evasion, more like she has decided the person asking isn't ready to hear the answer yet). Whether she actually sees something in what's coming, and how much, she has never said extensively.

She's reachable, she just picks who gets to reach her.

wikiNodes.title: Yellow Crown
wikiNodes.body:
The Yellow Crown is called a moon only by convention. Its carved sign of eldritch power turns Shivath into a dim, haunted echo of itself, where radiance becomes both revelation and punishment.

When the Yellow Crown is visible, the following effects apply to the world.

**Creatures**

- Whenever a creature deals radiant damage, that attack erupts in overcharged light.
- If the effect already has a radius, increase it by 5 feet.
- If it targets a point or a single creature, the radiant damage instead affects a 10-foot radius.
- Only the radiant portion expands; other riders or secondary effects do not.
- The creature that produced the radiant damage can also be caught in the burst.
- Art, literature, and music completed under the Yellow Crown become more beautiful and more corruptive. Anyone who studies or listens to such work for longer than 1 minute has disadvantage on their next saving throw against madness.
- Humanoids have advantage on saving throws against the frightened condition and disadvantage on death saving throws.

**Travel**

- The moon bathes the whole city in bright light that counts as both daylight and moonlight.
- Darkness becomes dim light, and dim light becomes bright light, even when the original darkness is magical.
- Stealth checks made while traveling take a -10 penalty.

**Madness**

- Characters who gain a madness under the Yellow Crown are flooded with visions of an older, truer city beyond the veil.
- The GM chooses a random location, character, or event and reveals information about it.
- Then the GM rolls 1d2:
  - On a 1, the information is true.
  - On a 2, the information is false.
- The character has no reliable way to tell which it is.
- Standard madness DC by average party level: 1-4 -> 11, 5-8 -> 13, 9-12 -> 15, 13-16 -> 17, 17-20 -> 19, 21+ -> 21.

**Short-Term**

- The character develops an obsessive fear of darkness.
- If they do not end their turn in bright light, they have disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws until the end of their next turn.
- If they start their turn outside bright light, they must use their movement to reach the nearest empty space in bright light.
- If they still are not in bright light after moving, they must use their action to Dash toward it.

**Long-Term**

- The character develops painful photophobia.
- If they end their turn in bright light, they must make a Constitution save against the madness DC or become poisoned for 1 minute, even if normally immune to that condition.
- 'Lesser restoration' and similar effects can end the poison, but renewed exposure can trigger it again.

**Indefinite**

- Roll 1d100.
- On 33 or lower, the character can shape the light around them into ephemeral wings and, if they start their turn in bright light, use a bonus action to gain a flying speed of 40 feet until the end of their next turn.
- On 34 or higher, they glow uncontrollably, shedding bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for another 10 feet.
- While glowing this way, they gain no benefit from finishing a short or long rest.

wikiNodes.title: Glacial Moon
wikiNodes.body:
When the frozen celestial body ascends to its place in the night sky, it conjures forth the very essence of winter, blanketing the world with an unyielding blizzard that saps warmth from bones and clarity from thoughts. Few dare to brave the frigid streets during this time, for the perils that lurk in the shadows are as merciless as the cold itself.

When the Glacial Moon is visible, the following effects apply to the world.

### **Monsters**

Monsters gain resistance to cold damage; if they already have this resistance, they become immune to cold damage instead.

They gain temporary hit points equal to their CR when the moon first rises (minimum of 1).

If an undead creature is hit with a melee attack while they have these temporary hit points, the attacker takes cold damage equal to the initial number of temporary hit points.

### **Travel**

The world is engulfed in a permanent blizzard that assaults the body and the mind and greatly limits visibility. Creatures other than monsters suffer a -10 penalty to Perception checks and their passive Perception scores. If they travel at a fast pace (as per the travel rules), they are considered blinded.

For each hour that passes, roll a d6. On a roll of 1, a strong blizzard wind rises. Each member of the party must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or take cold damage equal to their level. In addition, whenever this blizzard rises, the party must succeed on a DC 16 Survival check or get lost. If they are lost, the group’s travel time increases by two hours.

### **Madness**

The madness section of each moon refers to a Madness DC, which is indicated in the following table.

![9ddc593d-badc-4565-9347-93a104646263.png](https://d3a4xjr8r2ldhu.cloudfront.net/campaigns/276419/9ddc593d-badc-4565-9347-93a104646263.png)

  

The cold paired with the madness slows the body. If a character gains a madness, be it short, long, or indefinite, they must make a Constitution saving throw against the Madness DC or gain one point of exhaustion. Characters with resistance or immunity to cold damage automatically succeed on this saving throw.

#### **Short-Term**

Whenever a character gains a short-term madness under the Glacial Moon, their body numbs and they suffer a -1d4 penalty to all attack rolls and saving throws until the madness ends.

#### **Long-Term**

Whenever a character gains a long-term madness under the Glacial Moon, they feel compelled to suffer the cold to cleanse their body. Whenever they are in extreme cold, to better feel the merciless bite of the cold against their skin, they remove all their clothing, save for their undergarments, and refuse to dress up. This weakens their body, giving them disadvantage on Constitution checks and Constitution saving throws while in the cold environment. Characters that are immune to cold damage do not suffer this effect.

#### **Indefinite**

A character that gains an indefinite madness under the Glacial Moon becomes numb to the world around them.

Roll a d100;

on a result of 33 or lower, the character’s body becomes completely numb to all sensations, and they add their proficiency bonus to any Concentration checks and to any check made to endure pain.

On a result of 34 or higher, the character’s body suffers severe frostbite, numbing their nerves and body, crippling them. They have disadvantage on Dexterity checks and Dexterity saving throws, suffer disadvantage on all attack rolls made using Dexterity, and can’t add their Dexterity modifier to their Armor Class or initiative rolls. This eldritch frostbite can only be cured if the madness is removed.

They control hidden smuggling routes and conduct forbidden experiments tied to preserving humanity’s raw vitality, creating an air of mystery and unease around their operations. Their leaders, rarely seen, possess an almost otherworldly charisma and power, commanding absolute devotion from their followers. Mercenaries regard Iron Fang as both a lucrative employer and a deadly enemy, their payments reliable but their retribution swift and final for failure or betrayal.

Long ago it is said that a brave young Minotaur intentionally went within Daedalus with a ball of yarn, tying an end to it, this line of yarn acted like Hope itself, even when there seemed like there was no way out, Minos knew for the yarn was still connected to the outside, until it snapped.

There, it seemed like all hope was lost, Daedalus had destroyed the lifeline that Minos had so carefully laid out.

That is when Minos reached within himself, pulled on the divine energy that surrouded him and forged a ball of yarn that would be unseverable, and in that moment Minos and Daedalus were intrinsically connected.

From that point on, whether Minos was the first Minotaur or not, all Minotaurs since then have had an uncanny ability to escape and solve puzzles.

  

It is unknown whether Minos and Daedalus are seperate in their divinity.

wikiNodes.title: Sanguine Eclipse
wikiNodes.body:
The Sanguine Eclipse stains Shivath in a red haze that turns love into violence and fear into bloodlust. Under its glow, bonds of trust weaken first, and the closest hearts are the first ones the madness tries to break.

When the Sanguine Eclipse is visible, the following effects apply to the world.

**Creatures**

- Any creature that stays in direct moonlight for more than 1 minute at a time must make a Wisdom save against the madness DC or gain a short-term madness.
- Beasts gain advantage on attack rolls against frightened creatures.
- When a creature that is not already under the eclipse's influence sees an ally fall unconscious, it must make a Wisdom save against the madness DC.
- On a failure, the next time that witness falls unconscious because it hit 0 hit points, it starts with 2 failed death saves.
- That doom-laden curse lasts until the moon sets or until it is removed by 'remove curse' or similar magic.

**Travel**

- Streets are lit by a dim, bloody miasma.
- Traveling under open moonlight is nearly impossible unless the party can shield itself from direct exposure.

**Madness**

- Whenever a character gains a madness under the Sanguine Eclipse, they must make a Wisdom save against the madness DC or become frenzied for the duration of the madness or until the moon sets, whichever ends first.
- While frenzied, they see allies as enemies and spend their turns trying to kill them.
- The urge prioritizes the people they care about most.
- Characters immune to the charmed condition, or with advantage on saves against charm, have advantage on this frenzy save.
- Standard madness DC by average party level: 1-4 -> 11, 5-8 -> 13, 9-12 -> 15, 13-16 -> 17, 17-20 -> 19, 21+ -> 21.

**Short-Term**

- The character grows claws.
- Those claws can be used as unarmed strikes that deal 1d8 magical slashing damage and use Strength or Dexterity, whichever is higher.

**Long-Term**

- The character grows fangs.
- Once per turn, they can replace one melee attack with a fang attack that deals 1d6 magical piercing damage and grants temporary hit points equal to half the damage dealt.
- They also gain sunlight sensitivity for the duration.

**Indefinite**

- Roll 1d100.
- On 33 or lower, the character ignores the special madness effects of the Sanguine Eclipse until the current eclipse ends.
- On 34 or higher, their creature type becomes undead.
- When they hit with a fang attack, they may heal instead of gaining temporary hit points.
- They gain a compulsion to feed on humanoid blood. Each day they do not feed, they gain 1 level of exhaustion.
- They also gain a flying speed equal to their walking speed while they remain in darkness.

When your keys go missing, you might utter a prayer to nothing in particular or even to your own deity, and it might seem like those small prayers go nowhere, but they go to Bo Koltos, at least, that’s the last name that was last used.

Bo Koltos is the god of all that is lost and forgotten, both object and memories that leave the presence of people go to Bo Koltos, and Bo Koltos will try and return them to their rightful owners.

Bo Koltos ensures that nothing is truly forgotten, and when it is, Bo will return it, even those that are dead won’t be forgotten if Bo can ensure it.

Much like Bo’s domain, Bo is also prone to being forgotten by people, a solitary God trying to get everyone to remember that which they have lost.

wikiNodes.title: Creeping Tarlight
wikiNodes.body:
As the shadows thicken, the night air shudders under the eerie cackling of this sinister cosmic entity. The Creeping Tarlight, a moon emblazoned with a disquieting smile, projects its baleful grin upon Shivath. From its contorted face, a deluge of tar plummets, seeping from the moon's very countenance. As this glutinous substance permeates the land beneath, it imbues the city's darkness with an oppressive sense of dread, and its monsters with a viscous guile.  

As the Creeping Tarlight is visible, the following effects apply to the world:

### **Monsters**

The tar dripping from the moon causes shadows to become viscous and sticky. Creatures moving through areas of dim light or darkness have their speed halved, and they have disadvantage on initiative rolls while in dim light or darkness.

  
 

All monsters, apart from humanoids, are coated in tar. The first time a tar-coated creature takes fire or radiant damage, it explodes. Each creature within 10 feet of an exploding creature must make a Trait DC Dexterity saving throw or take fire damage equal to the Trait Damage. The tar-coated creature has disadvantage on the saving throw.

  
 

The influence of the Creeping Tarlight causes curses and hexes to become sticky and difficult to remove. Even if dispelled, the tar-like residue of the curse may linger, causing persistent effects. All spells that cause curses have their duration doubled and cannot be removed by the remove curse spell while the moon is up.

  
 

![9ddc574d-cbb4-4f7c-9134-4e4c668613fc.png](https://d3a4xjr8r2ldhu.cloudfront.net/campaigns/276419/9ddc574d-cbb4-4f7c-9134-4e4c668613fc.png)

### **Travel**

Under the sinister grin of the Creeping Tarlight, the atmosphere is permeated with unease and the lingering aroma of viscous sludge. Darkness intensifies, stretching inky tendrils across the night, while the pallid, twisted smile of the moon stands out against the void. This deceptive gloom masks the true threat of the encroaching tar, engulfing those who fail to tread with caution. The eerie smile on the moon occasionally emits a faint, disturbing laughter that can be heard throughout the night. This unsettling sound makes it increasingly difficult for creatures to relax their mind, as the sound emerges from everywhere at once. If characters finish a long rest during a night where the Creeping Tarlight is visible, they must succeed on a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw to gain the benefits. In addition, the tar that drips from the moons risks engulfing the unwary in its inky depths. For each hour that passes, roll a d6. On a 1, the party becomes trapped in a heavily shadowed area, generated from the tar of the moon. Each character must succeed on a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw or fall in the darkness and be restrained. If the party traveled at a slow pace (as per the travel rules), the characters have advantage on this saving throw. On their turn, as part of their movement, a trapped character can escape by making a DC 17 Strength check. Another creature can use an action to make a DC 17 Strength check to attempt to pull the restrained character out of the shadows, freeing them on a success. After 2 turns, the trapped character begins to suffocate in the tar, and after 3 turns, the trapped character is completely engulfed; any creature that attempts to free the character will get coated in tar. Alternatively, the shadowy tar can be lit ablaze with fire damage, which burns for 1 minute. For the duration, any creature in contact with the tar takes 2d6 fire damage at the start of each of its turns. 

### **Madness**

The madness section of each moon refers to a Madness DC, which is indicated in the following table. 

![9ddc57a1-e858-4a3c-ba2b-2fc6528c8e77.png](https://d3a4xjr8r2ldhu.cloudfront.net/campaigns/276419/9ddc57a1-e858-4a3c-ba2b-2fc6528c8e77.png)

 The tar slugs the body and the mind. If a character gains a madness while the Creeping Tarlight is out, for the duration of the madness, their speed is halved, they take a -2 penalty to AC and Dexterity saving throws, and they can’t use reactions. 

#### **Short-Term**

Whenever a character gains a short-term madness under the Creeping Tarlight, they burst into a frenzied laughter. For the duration of the madness, they automatically fail any Stealth check they make, and all creatures in a 120-foot radius are alerted to their presence. 

#### **Long-Term**

Whenever a character gains a long-term madness under the Creeping Tarlight, the demented laughter that grips their mind becomes untenable. For the duration of the madness, they find the darkest of things profoundly amusing. If they attempt to speak or cast a spell with a verbal component, they must succeed on a Madness DC Constitution saving throw to steady themselves or be unable to talk or cast the spell, wasting their action but not the spell slot, and instead giggle and smile.  
 If one of their allies is reduced to 0 hit points, they explode with laughter, completely losing their focus, and are stunned until the start of their next turn. 

#### **Indefinite**

A character that gains an indefinite madness under the Creeping Tarlight finds inner joy, and the laughter quiets. **Roll a d100:**

on a result of 33 or lower, the character begins to laugh and regurgitate tar, which completely coats their body, acting like a battle armor, and their AC increases by 1on a result of 34 or higher, the tar solidifies too much, and the character becomes petrified, their face frozen in a terrifying smile. Ending the petrification also ends the indefinite madness.

wikiNodes.title: Shattered Moon
wikiNodes.body:
<!-- content-meta:eyJzdXBwcmVzc2VkTWVudGlvbnMiOlsidHJhdmVsIiwidW5kZWFkLW1uM3JoenRxIiwibWFkbmVzcyIsImx1bmFyIiwibGlnaHQiXX0= -->

No one speaks with certainty about what the Shattered Moon once was, only that its destruction changed everything around it. Its broken light is strangely calm, but the fragments it sheds still hunger to become whole again.

When the Shattered Moon is visible, the following effects apply to the world.

**Creatures**

- Creatures have advantage on Stealth checks.
- Creatures have disadvantage on Perception checks.
- Humanoids have advantage on saving throws against madness.

**Travel**

- The world is washed in a soft, almost peaceful moonlight.
- Each hour of travel, roll 1d4. On a 1, a lunar shower begins for 1d6 x 10 minutes.
- During that shower, ephemeral shards of light fall across Shivath.
- Contact with that rain dispels spells of 5th level or lower, ends concentration, and halves the range of magic to a minimum of 5 feet.
- Creatures with passive Perception 15 or higher can notice the shower one minute before it begins.

**Geistnacht**

- When the moon first appears, roll 1d4.
- On a 1, the night becomes a Geistnacht.
- The moon shatters in complete silence, and spirits descend looking for souls to harvest.
- During a Geistnacht, each hour of travel uses a d6 encounter roll; on a 1-2, the party encounters hostile undead.
- The party can avoid them with a group Stealth check against the highest passive Perception among those undead.
- On a failure, roll 1d4 instead of 1d6 for the next hour of travel.
- If the party fails by 5 or more, the undead notice them immediately.

**Madness**

- The Shattered Moon has lost much of its original aura, but it still tries to mend itself with borrowed life.
- Standard madness DC by average party level: 1-4 -> 11, 5-8 -> 13, 9-12 -> 15, 13-16 -> 17, 17-20 -> 19, 21+ -> 21.

**Short-Term**

- At the start of each turn, the character takes 1d6 necrotic damage.
- Any magical healing ends that recurring damage.

**Long-Term**

- The moon's influence breaks a limb.
- The character takes 2d6 necrotic damage and rolls 1d4:
  - 1: right arm unusable.
  - 2: left arm unusable.
  - 3: right leg unusable.
  - 4: left leg unusable.
- A broken arm prevents holding anything with two hands and limits the character to one held object at a time.
- A broken leg reduces base walking speed to 5 feet, though a crutch or cane can restore movement to half the original speed if the other leg still works.
- The limb cannot be treated while the moon remains visible.
- After the moon sets, a healing spell of 4th level or higher can restore it.

**Indefinite**

- Roll 1d100.
- On 33 or lower, the moon fails to feed and instead strips away madness. The character is cured of all madness currently affecting them.
- On 34 or higher, the moon devours the character's body. They take 10d6 + 40 necrotic damage, and if this reduces them to 0 hit points, they disintegrate into drifting particles of light.

wikiNodes.title: Krakenlight
wikiNodes.body:
When tendrils spread across the face of the moon, Shivath falls beneath the Krakenlight. Water hangs in the sky like a suspended sea, rain floods the streets, and creatures of the deep blur the boundary between ocean and air.

When the Krakenlight is visible, the following effects apply to the world.

**Monsters**

- Aberrations and humanoids become slick and slimy; spells and magical effects cannot restrain them.
- Those creatures can spend 5 feet of movement to escape nonmagical restraints automatically.
- Being underwater no longer imposes penalties on their movement or attacks.
- Monsters with a swimming speed of 30 feet or higher gain a flying speed equal to that swimming speed.
- If one of those flying creatures is reduced to 0 speed, it falls upward toward the sky-sea instead of downward.
- Aberrations gain **Bioluminescent Lure**:
  - As an action, the creature creates a dim light in a 10-foot radius above itself.
  - A creature that sees the lure must make a Wisdom save against the monster's trait DC or become charmed for 1 minute, moving toward the light and ending movement inside it whenever possible.
  - The charm ends if the target takes damage.

**Trait DC by CR**

| CR | DC |
| --- | --- |
| 2 or lower | 10 |
| 3-4 | 12 |
| 5-6 | 14 |
| 7-8 | 16 |
| 9-12 | 17 |
| 13-16 | 18 |
| 17-20 | 19 |
| 21+ | 20 |

**Travel**

- Travel pace is halved beneath the constant rain.
- Finishing a long rest without cover from the rain requires a DC 12 Constitution save to gain the rest's benefits.
- Rain lightly obscures uncovered areas, extinguishes open flames, and imposes disadvantage on Perception checks that rely on sight or hearing.
- Each hour of travel, roll 1d12. On a 1, a tentacle descends nearby.
- A creature can grab the tentacle with a DC 14 Athletics check.
- If anyone holds on, roll 1d6:
  - On 1-5, the tentacle drags them 1,000 feet in a random direction before vanishing, and they take 5d6 falling damage.
  - On 6, it drags them into the sky-ocean.

**Madness**

- Whenever a character succeeds on a saving throw against madness under the Krakenlight, they vent that strain as a 15-foot-radius cloud of ink centered on themselves. The area is heavily obscured until the end of that character's next turn.
- Standard madness DC by average party level: 1-4 -> 11, 5-8 -> 13, 9-12 -> 15, 13-16 -> 17, 17-20 -> 19, 21+ -> 21.

**Short-Term**

- The character is mesmerized by the storm above, falls prone, and their speed becomes 0 until the end of their next turn.

**Long-Term**

- At the start of each turn in combat, roll 1d4.
- On a 1, the character's body twists in impossible angles; their speed is halved and they have disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws until the start of their next turn.

**Indefinite**

- Roll 1d100.
- On 33 or lower, the character gains the effects of 'freedom of movement', but if they take lightning damage they become paralyzed until the start of their next turn.
- On 34 or higher, their body mutates with fins and gills. They must remain underwater to breathe or speak, or they begin to choke.

wikiNodes.title: Scorching Moon
wikiNodes.body:
The Scorching Moon hangs over Shivath like a burning omen. Most of the fire it brings is illusory, but the false inferno hides real columns of flame that erupt without warning and punish anyone who cannot tell fear from danger.

When the Scorching Moon is visible, the following effects apply to the world.

**Monsters**

- Monsters gain resistance to fire damage. If they already have that resistance, they become immune instead.
- Their melee weapon attacks deal extra fire damage equal to their CR, minimum 1.
- Beasts gain **Fire Charge**:
  - If the beast moves at least 20 feet straight toward a creature and then hits it with a melee attack on the same turn, that target must make a Strength save.
  - On a failure, the target falls prone and takes extra fire damage based on the beast's CR.

**Fire Charge by CR**

| CR | Save DC | Extra Damage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 or lower | 10 | 1d4 |
| 3-4 | 10 | 1d6 |
| 5-6 | 11 | 2d6 |
| 7-8 | 11 | 3d6 |
| 9-12 | 12 | 4d6 |
| 13-16 | 13 | 5d6 |
| 17-20 | 14 | 6d6 |
| 21+ | 15 | 7d6 |

**Travel**

- Shivath is filled with soot, heat, and walls of false fire.
- Each hour of travel, roll 1d6. On a 1, a real column of flame erupts beneath the party.
- Each character must make a DC 14 Dexterity save or take fire damage equal to their level.
- A creature that has experienced the moon before may make a DC 14 Survival check instead, picking its way through illusion and flame.
- A party moving at a slow pace has advantage on these checks and saves, and may attempt the Survival check even on a first encounter.

**Madness**

- If a character takes fire damage equal to their level or higher in a single turn, they must make a Wisdom save against the madness DC or gain a short-term madness.
- Standard madness DC by average party level: 1-4 -> 11, 5-8 -> 13, 9-12 -> 15, 13-16 -> 17, 17-20 -> 19, 21+ -> 21.

**Short-Term**

- The character catches fire, taking 1d4 fire damage at the start of each of their turns.
- Their melee attacks deal an extra 1d4 fire damage.
- The flames end after 1 minute or if the character or an adjacent creature uses an action to douse them.

**Long-Term**

- Whenever the character sees an open flame larger than 1 foot across, such as a bonfire, they must make a Wisdom save against the madness DC or become charmed by it.
- While charmed in this way, they are incapacitated and their speed becomes 0.
- The effect ends if they take damage or if another creature uses an action to shake them free.
- Once a character succeeds against one specific flame, or the effect ends for them, they are immune to that flame for 24 hours.

**Indefinite**

- Roll 1d100.
- On 33 or lower, the character gains resistance to fire damage.
- On 34 or higher, the character gains vulnerability to fire damage.
- The result lasts until the madness is cured.

wikiNodes.title: Slumbering Moon
wikiNodes.body:
The Slumbering Moon looks almost ordinary, which makes it all the more dangerous. Its reflection twists memory, distance, and intention until Shivath feels less like a place and more like a dream that refuses to let anyone wake up.

When the Slumbering Moon is visible, the following effects apply to the world.

**Creatures**

- A creature that can see the moon may use its action to study the reflection hidden inside it and make a DC 19 Intelligence check.
- On a success, it teleports as if it had cast 'dimension door'.
- On a failure, it gains a short-term madness, teleports randomly to an empty space within 500 feet, and gains resistance to falling damage until the end of its turn.
- Aberrations automatically succeed on this check.

**Travel**

- Any character who has seen the moon, even indirectly or in a painting, falls under its influence.
- If such a character leaves Shivath, the next long rest returns them to a familiar place within the city.
- If they are unfamiliar with Shivath, they wake in a random street.
- A character that goes 24 hours after leaving the city without finishing a long rest falls unconscious, even if normally immune to that condition.
- When they wake, they remember nothing about leaving the city or wanting to do so.
- Anyone else who knew about those plans also has their memories altered into a more mundane explanation.
- Every time this affliction triggers after the first, the character must make a Wisdom save against the madness DC. On a failure, they gain a long-term madness; on a success, they gain a short-term one.
- This curse can be ended only by 'wish' or by banishing the moon itself.

**Madness**

- Standard madness DC by average party level: 1-4 -> 11, 5-8 -> 13, 9-12 -> 15, 13-16 -> 17, 17-20 -> 19, 21+ -> 21.

**Short-Term**

- The character forgets how to use part of what they know.
- They lose proficiency with a weapon, or become unable to cast one spell they know or have prepared, chosen by the GM.

**Long-Term**

- Memory continues to erode.
- The character has disadvantage on Arcana, History, and Religion checks.

**Indefinite**

- The character permanently loses the ability to remember anything that happens while the madness lasts.
- If the madness ends, the time spent under it remains gone from memory.

wikiNodes.title: Vacuous Moon
wikiNodes.body:
<!-- content-meta:eyJzdXBwcmVzc2VkTWVudGlvbnMiOlsibGlnaHQiLCJtYWRuZXNzIiwidHJhdmVsIl19 -->

The Vacuous Moon is less a moon than a wound in the sky. It swallows light, thins the barrier between the living world and the dead, and fills Shivath with chained apparitions that only the unlucky can fully perceive.

When the Vacuous Moon is visible, the following effects apply to the world.

**Monsters**

- Monsters of CR 5 or lower are blinded.
- Monsters gain blindsight out to 30 feet.
- Monsters have advantage on Perception checks that rely on hearing or smell.
- Monstrosities gain **Void Step**: after taking damage from a ranged attack, they can use their reaction to teleport to an empty space within 5 feet of the attacker and make one melee weapon attack.

**Travel**

- Torches barely cut through the filth-dark streets.
- If a character stares directly at the moon for more than 6 seconds, they must make a Wisdom save against the madness DC or gain a short-term madness.
- The first time each day a character gains the ability to see invisible creatures or objects, they are compelled to stare at the moon for one round.

**Vacuous Light**

- Darkvision does not function.
- Dim light becomes darkness.
- A creature that can see invisible creatures and objects does not suffer disadvantage on Perception checks due to darkness.
- Creatures have disadvantage on saving throws against madness while they are not in bright light.

**Madness**

- Whenever a character fails a Wisdom saving throw while the Vacuous Moon is visible, they gain one short-term madness. Saves made directly against madness do not trigger this extra effect.
- Standard madness DC by average party level: 1-4 -> 11, 5-8 -> 13, 9-12 -> 15, 13-16 -> 17, 17-20 -> 19, 21+ -> 21.

**Short-Term**

- The character is under the effect of 'see invisibility'.
- What they see are the shadowy, upside-down shapes of lost loved ones hanging in chains and drifting toward the moon.
- The terror leaves them frightened for the duration.

**Long-Term**

- The spectral figures become almost indistinguishable from reality.
- The character remains under 'see invisibility' and has disadvantage on all attack rolls because they cannot reliably tell real from unreal.
- A blinded creature does not suffer this attack penalty.

**Indefinite**

- Roll 1d100.
- On 33 or lower, the character can cast 'blink' on themselves at will without components, but if they use it three times in a day they return permanently blinded.
- On 34 or higher, figures from their past tear out the character's eyes and vanish into the void with them, leaving the character permanently blinded.

wikiNodes.title: Aarakocra
wikiNodes.body:
## Flight

Because of your wings, you have a flying speed equal to your walking speed. You can't use this flying speed if you're wearing medium or heavy armor.

## Talons

You have talons that you can use to make unarmed strikes. When you hit with them, the strike deals 1d6 + your Strength modifier slashing damage, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

## Wind Caller

Starting at 3rd level, you can cast the gust of wind spell with this trait, without requiring a material component. Once you cast the spell with this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have of 2nd level or higher.

Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for when you cast gust of wind with this trait (choose when you select this race).

wikiNodes.title: Nejbet
wikiNodes.body:
<!-- content-meta:eyJzdWJ0aXRsZSI6IlRoZSBDcm93biBvZiBEdXN0LCBUaGUgU3VubGVzcyBNb3RoZXIiLCJwcm9ub3VucyI6IlNoZS9oZXIiLCJnZW5kZXIiOiJEZW1pZ2lybCIsInR5cGUiOiJQYXRyb24gKFVuZGVhZCkgLyBQYXRyb24gKENlbGVzdGlhbCkifQ== -->

**Nejbet** was the last queen of the ancient kingdom once known as **Akharet**, now buried beneath the sand and remembered as **Nejab**. She is remembered as a ruler of great ambition, revered especially in rites of birth, war, and coronation: central elements of her people's culture. Many ancient texts referred to her as the _“Mother of the Sun”_ and the “Crown of the Upper Lands” (though she no longer identifies with either title).

Nejbet is most widely remembered for her attempt to grant her people immortality through a forgotten ritual known only as **the Seven Words**. According to her followers, the ritual failed... Or was sabotaged. Nejbet herself claims she was **betrayed by those closest to her**, and that the result was her transformation into a being of many bodies and a fragmented soul. She now exists as a **hive of unliving forms** — the dead of Akharet — which she controls, but from which she cannot truly escape.

Though no longer mortal, nor fully divine, Nejbet’s voice still echoes in her forgotten ruins, and through warlocks who claim her as their patron. When she speaks, she talks of a **vessel** created from the essence of her people, of **someone who stole what should have been hers**, and of a path to reclaim what was lost.
